title: 塞下曲·其三（月黑雁飞高）
author: 卢纶
intro: A moonless night, geese startled into the sky, the enemy chief slipping away — and Tang cavalry about to give chase, their bows and swords heavy with snow.
analysis: 这首诗写唐军雪夜追击敌人的场面。第一句写环境：没有月亮的黑夜，大雁被惊动，高高飞起——为什么大雁会惊飞？因为有人在黑暗中偷偷行动。第二句点明：原来是敌军首领单于趁着夜色逃跑了。后两句写唐军：将领正要带领轻骑兵去追，一转眼，大雪已经落满了弓和刀。诗在这里戛然而止，没有写追击的经过和结果，只停在出发前的一瞬间，却让人感受到将士们不怕严寒、勇往直前的气势。“大雪满弓刀”五个字，既写出了天气的严寒，又写出了战士整装待发的英武形象，画面感极强。短短二十个字，写出一场紧张的边塞夜战。
analysisEn: This poem shows Tang troops about to chase the enemy on a snowy night. Line one sets the scene: a moonless night, and wild geese flying up high — why would geese take off in the dark? Because something is moving secretly below. Line two explains: the chanyu, the enemy chief, is fleeing under cover of night. The second half turns to the Tang side: the commander is about to lead light cavalry after him, and in that moment heavy snow has already covered their bows and swords. The poem stops right there. It doesn’t tell us about the chase or how it ended — it freezes the instant before they ride out — yet we feel the soldiers’ courage and their disregard for the cold. The last line, 大雪满弓刀, does two jobs at once: it shows how bitter the weather is, and it gives us a striking picture of warriors ready to charge. Twenty characters, and a whole tense night battle on the frontier.
background: Lu Lun (c. 739–c. 799) was one of the “Ten Talents of the Dali Era” of the mid-Tang and spent time on the staff of frontier commanders. “Frontier Song” is a set of six poems written in reply to a general; this is the third.
pronunciation: 单于 chán yú（古代匈奴首领的称号，不读 dān；机器朗读可能读错，已在“朗读用字”换成同音字“蝉”）；遁逃 dùn；将 jiāng（带领）。轻骑：统编教材注 qí（2016 年审音后“骑”统读 qí），旧读 jì。
version: 采用统编教材（四年级下册）文本。组诗原题《和张仆射塞下曲》，共六首，这是第三首。

lines.lit: The moon is dark; geese fly high;
lines.en: No moon tonight — the geese fly high;

lines.lit: the chanyu flees in the night.
lines.en: the enemy chief is slipping away in the dark.

lines.lit: About to lead light cavalry in pursuit,
lines.en: Just as we mount to ride him down,

lines.lit: heavy snow fills bows and swords.
lines.en: deep snow lies heavy on our bows and blades.

words.en: chanyu, title of the Xiongnu ruler
words.note: 读 chán yú，这里泛指敌军首领。

words.en: to be about to; to want to
words.note: 现代汉语“欲望”“跃跃欲试”。
古义“率领”，和今天的“将要”不同。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 无月的黑夜，为敌人逃跑提供了掩护，也营造出紧张的气氛。
imagery.en: A moonless night gives the enemy cover to escape and makes the mood tense.

imagery.name: 雁
imagery.zh: 大雁在黑夜中高飞，是被逃跑的敌军惊起的，暗示了敌情。
imagery.en: Geese flying high in the dark have been startled by the fleeing enemy — a silent signal that something is happening.

imagery.name: 雪
imagery.zh: 大雪落满弓刀，写出边塞的严寒，更衬托出将士不畏艰苦、准备出击的英勇。
imagery.en: Snow piling on bows and swords shows the frontier’s bitter cold — and the soldiers’ courage as they ride out anyway.
